# vendor

Pdfium, downloaded here. Nothing in this folder is in git — this note is the exception, and the only
thing that is (see the end of `.gitignore`).

The app **loads** Pdfium at run time rather than linking against it (see `src/pdfium/`), which is why
the library has to be *somewhere* rather than being built into the executable:

```text
vendor/
    lib/pdfium.dll          the library the app loads, and the one a build copies next to the exe
    include/*.h             the C headers that library was built with — the ABI this app declares
    VERSION                 which Pdfium build it is
    args.gn                 the GN arguments that build was made with
    LICENSE, licenses/      Pdfium's own licences, carried with it
```

## The build in this folder

**PDFium 158.0.8125.0** — `pdfium-binaries` release `chromium/8125`, published 2026-10-26 and
downloaded 2026-10-27.

| | |
|---|---|
| Archive | `pdfium-win-x64.tgz` from <https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries/releases/tag/chromium%2F8125> |
| Archive SHA-256 | `9a964261760cff52570aabf038ab346d3a5034dd8b30d0d5fe8861235d356b8b` |
| `lib/pdfium.dll` SHA-256 | `4b0dec92555d69437bef0df37be630181ab3e83a6823ca264ede355a4f2ef994` |
| Built with | x64, release, **no V8, no XFA** (`args.gn`) |

The import library in the release (`lib/pdfium.dll.lib`) is deliberately not copied: the app resolves
its entry points with `GetProcAddress` and never links against Pdfium.

## Where it comes from

A **`pdfium-binaries`** release: prebuilt Pdfium for Windows, from
<https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries/releases> — `pdfium-win-x64.tgz` (or the archive for the
machine). Its own layout is this one: unpack `bin/pdfium.dll` into `vendor/lib/`, and `include/`,
`VERSION`, `args.gn` and the licences beside it.

The stability promise this wrapper relies on is Pdfium's own: the files in its `public/` directory
are the API for embedders, and code outside it may change at any time
(<https://pdfium.googlesource.com/pdfium/+/refs/heads/main/README.md>). That is why
`src/pdfium/api.rs` names only public entry points, and only the ones the app calls.

**The headers matter as much as the library.** `FPDF_GetPageSizeByIndexF` takes an `FS_SIZEF*`; the
older `FPDF_GetPageSizeByIndex` beside it takes two `double*`s. `src/pdfium/api.rs` declares what
`vendor/include` says — a library from a build whose header differs may load and then write the wrong
size through the wrong pointer. That is why the headers are vendored with the library rather than
generated by a binding for "some" Pdfium version.

## Updating it

1. Pick the newest `chromium/<build>` release on the `pdfium-binaries` releases page and read its
   `VERSION` and `args.gn`. This app wants a Windows **x64** archive.
2. Download `pdfium-win-x64.tgz`, verify the SHA-256 GitHub publishes for the asset, and unpack it.
3. Copy it over this folder:
   ```powershell
   $new = 'C:\path\to\extracted\pdfium'
   Copy-Item "$new\bin\pdfium.dll" vendor\lib\pdfium.dll -Force
   Copy-Item "$new\include\*" vendor\include -Recurse -Force
   Copy-Item "$new\licenses\*" vendor\licenses -Force
   Copy-Item "$new\LICENSE", "$new\VERSION", "$new\args.gn" vendor -Force
   ```
4. Run `cargo test`. The wrapper resolves thirty-two symbols and checks the C layouts it uses, and
   `pdf::tests` renders real fixtures: a public-header change shows up there rather than in a release
   build. Diff `vendor/include` against the previous headers before accepting the update — the
   declarations in `src/pdfium/api.rs` follow those files, not a binding for another version.

`build.rs` watches `vendor/VERSION` and `vendor/lib`, so an update is noticed by the next build.

## What a build does with it

`build.rs` copies `vendor/lib/*.dll` next to the executable a build produces, so
`target/release/cheap-note.exe` and `pdfium.dll` are a pair that can be started from anywhere or copied
to another machine. A build with no `vendor/lib` says so as a warning, and the app it produces runs
without PDF support — a state the app is designed for: it starts, draws, writes ink, and refuses to
open a PDF with a message rather than a crash.
